entities.summary:
Enrico Minutoli was an Italian Cardinal born in the late 14th century and died on June 26, 1412. He played a crucial role in the Catholic Church during the tumultuous Middle Ages. As a key figure in the papal election of 1409, which led to the Western Schism, Minutoli's influence extended beyond Italy to shape European politics and theology.

During his tenure as Cardinal-Dean of the College of Cardinals, he was instrumental in promoting theological reform and advocating for the authority of the papacy. His efforts contributed to the development of a more centralized and hierarchical church structure, which would have lasting impacts on Catholicism.

Despite his significant contributions to the Church, Minutoli's legacy is also marked by controversy. His support for the Avignon Papacy and his involvement in the sale of indulgences during the Black Death exacerbated tensions between the papacy and European monarchies.

One striking statistic from Minutoli's time is that the average life expectancy in Europe during the 14th century was just 35 years, highlighting the devastating impact of the pandemic on populations. This tragic event left an indelible mark on Minutoli's worldview, shaping his views on mortality, faith, and the human condition.

In conclusion, Enrico Minutoli's life and legacy serve as a testament to the complex and often fraught history of the Catholic Church during the Middle Ages. As a key player in this pivotal era, his influence extended far beyond Italy, leaving an enduring impact on European politics, theology, and culture.
